name: Natural Material Stress Reduction via Multi-Modal Sensory Convergence
short_description: Natural materials (especially wood) produce stress reduction through convergence of visual-fractal, haptic-thermal, acoustic, olfactory, and ecological channels
structural_pattern: Natural materials — particularly wood, but also natural stone, earth, and plant fibers — produce stress-reduction effects that exceed any single sensory channel's contribution. The effect arises from CONVERGENCE: (1) Visual: natural grain patterns exhibit 1/f spectral profiles (T1); (2) Haptic-thermal: low thermal effusivity maintains skin-temperature contact (MAT1); (3) Acoustic: moderate absorption produces warm acoustics (AX1); (4) Olfactory: VOCs (terpenes) activate olfactory-limbic pathways reducing sympathetic activity; (5) Ecological: natural signatures match statistical regularities the brain is calibrated to. Each channel contributes modest stress reduction; the convergent total is larger than any single channel, and potentially super-additive.
higher_order_principle: Material-domain instantiation of the multi-channel convergence principle (like L3 for daylight). As daylight engages multiple channels simultaneously, natural materials engage visual-fractal, haptic-thermal, acoustic, olfactory, and ecological channels simultaneously. Multi-channel confirmation produces qualitatively greater processing fluency.

convergent_channels.name: visual_fractal
convergent_channels.mechanism: 1/f grain patterns near D≈1.3 → processing fluency

convergent_channels.name: haptic_thermal
convergent_channels.mechanism: Low effusivity → skin-temp maintenance → CT activation

convergent_channels.name: acoustic
convergent_channels.mechanism: Moderate absorption → warm, intimate room acoustics

convergent_channels.name: ecological
convergent_channels.mechanism: Natural signatures match brain's ecological heuristics

wood_optimal_ratio: ~45% wood surface ratio (Tsunetsugu et al., 2007) — inverted-U function

wood_channel_weights.note: Expert-estimated weights from Panel MAT-II — preliminary, awaiting 2×2×2 factorial validation

visual_grain_fractal.mechanism: Natural grain patterns with fractal dimension D≈1.3 → processing fluency (T1)
visual_grain_fractal.evidence: Strongest empirical base; operates continuously; most easily replicated by imitation (wood-grain laminates)
visual_grain_fractal.source: Taylor et al. (2011); Nyrud & Bringslimark (2010); Miyazaki visual-only d≈0.3–0.5

haptic_thermal.mechanism: Low effusivity → skin-temp maintenance → CT-afferent activation (MAT1)
haptic_thermal.evidence: Strong theoretical basis from CT-afferent literature; intermittent contact pattern (~5–10% of waking time)
haptic_thermal.source: McGlone et al. (2014); Sakuragawa et al. (2005)

acoustic_absorption.mechanism: Moderate absorption (α≈0.05–0.15) → warm, intimate room acoustics (AX1)
acoustic_absorption.evidence: Real but small relative to dedicated acoustic treatments; contribution primarily through ABSENCE of harsh reflections

olfactory_vocs.evidence: Miyazaki estimates 25–35% contribution during first 5 minutes; d≈0.4–0.7 on autonomic measures
olfactory_vocs.time_dependency: HIGH at arrival (first 5 min), near-ZERO after 15–20 min due to adaptation
olfactory_vocs.note: TIME-AVERAGED weight; resets at each transition (OLF1 transition function)
olfactory_vocs.source: Ikei et al. (2017); Dalton (2000) on olfactory adaptation

biophilic_cultural.mechanism: Natural signatures match brain's ecological heuristics; cultural familiarity (MAT5)
biophilic_cultural.cultural_variation: Higher in strong wood traditions (Japan, Scandinavia); lower where stone/earth is dominant natural material

super_additivity.meaning: Full wood convergence effect exceeds sum of individual channel contributions by 20–30%
super_additivity.comparison: Higher than L3 daylight (15–25%) because material convergence involves more independent sensory modalities
super_additivity.falsification: If < 10%, convergence model adds little; if > 40%, interaction terms dominate

time_structure.visual: Continuous (100% of waking time eyes open in space)
time_structure.haptic: Intermittent (contact with handrails, desks, doors ~5–10% of time)
time_structure.olfactory: Transitional (high at arrival, adapts to near-zero after 15–20 min)

non_wood_material_profiles.note: PRELIMINARY expert judgment from Panel MAT-II; not empirically calibrated

notes.visual: Mineral texture, geological layering, color variation (crystalline rather than organic structure)
notes.haptic_thermal: High effusivity creates sustained coolness; CLIMATE-DEPENDENT valence (positive in hot, negative in cold)
notes.acoustic: High reflectivity creates characteristic reverberation; LARGER contribution than wood

notes.visual: Surface texture (formwork marks, aggregate exposure); DOMINANT channel — quality varies enormously with craftsmanship
notes.olfactory: Near-zero in cured state (exception: Zumthor's Bruder Klaus Chapel char-olfactory)
notes.cultural: HIGHLY POLARIZING: modernity, brutalism, institutional austerity vs. artisanal craft

notes.visual: Reflectivity, color (steel gray, copper green, brass gold); specular vs. matte
notes.haptic_thermal: Very high effusivity (b>7,000) creates strong cold sensation; typically AVERSIVE in cold conditions
notes.acoustic: Distinctive resonance; STRONGEST acoustic identity of any material class
notes.cultural: Technology, precision, industry, modernity; less polarizing than concrete

channel_factorial_experiment.design: 2×2×2 (visual wood vs non-wood × haptic wood vs non-wood × olfactory wood vs non-wood)
channel_factorial_experiment.controls: Acoustic and ambient thermal held constant
predictions: Each channel produces main effect on autonomic parasympathetic activation (visual d≈0.3–0.5, haptic d≈0.3–0.6, olfactory d≈0.4–0.7)
Three-channel combination exceeds sum by 20–30% (super-additivity test)
Visual × haptic interaction is largest two-way interaction (highest prior precision)
Olfactory shows TIME × CHANNEL interaction: large at 0–5 min, near-zero at 20+ min
channel_factorial_experiment.falsification: If no super-additivity observed, convergence model is wrong; if olfactory shows no time-dependent adaptation, OLF1 transition model needs revision
channel_factorial_experiment.status: NOT YET CONDUCTED — highest priority experiment

calibration_parameters.calibration_source: Panel MAT-II (Doc 51) — Spence, Miyazaki, Pallasmaa channel estimation

causal_links.evidence_base: T1 mechanism: 1/f spectral profile of natural grain → fractal fluency → positive affect. (Spehar et al., 2003; Taylor et al., 2011)
MAT1 pathway: wood e~400 → skin-temperature maintenance → CT activation → insular comfort signal.
AX1/AX4: wood has moderate absorption (α ~0.1–0.3), producing warm acoustics.
Miyazaki's phytoncide pathway: wood terpenes → olfactory → limbic → reduced sympathetic activity. Li et al. (2006, 2009).
Convergence hypothesis: simultaneous confirmation across channels produces greater stress reduction than sum of individual channels. Material analog of L3 daylight convergence.

scope_conditions: Applies to environments with substantial natural material surfaces — proportion matters (peak at ~45%)
VOC pathway requires UNTREATED or lightly treated natural material
Convergence applies to genuine natural materials, not simulated — laminate engages visual only and may produce MAT3 PE
Cultural moderation: effect demonstrated primarily in Japanese and Scandinavian populations
moderators: Material proportion: inverted-U — too little → insufficient signal; too much → visual monotony
Surface treatment: sealants block VOCs and change thermal properties
Wood species: terpene profiles differ (hinoki, cedar, pine)
Exposure duration: visual/haptic effects rapid; olfactory-autonomic effects build over hours
Building age: new wood releases more VOCs; aged wood develops richer visual/haptic complexity

interactions.nature: T1 is the visual channel of MAT4. Natural grain patterns engage T1.
MAT1 is the haptic-thermal channel of MAT4.
AX1 is the acoustic channel of MAT4.
MAT4 and L3 are structural analogs: multi-channel convergence. L3 = daylight; MAT4 = natural materials.
MAT3 describes cross-modal prediction machinery. MAT4 describes what happens when natural materials PASS all MAT3 checks — full convergence produces 'realness' signal.
